intro.Subject: Subject of Proverbs: Words of Wisdom Teaching People How to Behave and How to Build Up Their Character in the Human Life
intro.Author: The main writers and collectors are Solomon (1:1; 10:1; 25:1; cf. 1 Kings 4:32; Eccl. 12:9) and Hezekiah (25:1), who added some proverbs of the forefathers in chs. 25—29. Chapter 30 is attributed to Agur, and ch. 31 to King Lemuel; nothing definite is known concerning either man.
intro.Time of Writing: About 1000 B.C. (Solomon's portion, chs. 1—24) and about 700 B.C. (Hezekiah's portion, chs. 25—29). The time of writing for chs. 30—31 is unknown.

footnotes.text:
Heb. mishle, meaning similitudes, proverbs, parables, to represent general truths. Proverbs is a collection of the words of the wise. It stresses the wisdom that man receives of God through his contacting of God and that teaches man how to behave and build up his character in his human life. Since the proverbs were collected mainly by two kings of Judah (Solomon and Hezekiah) in the age of the law, the book of Proverbs may be considered a subsidiary to the law. The law is the portrait of God; as such, it demands that God’s people keep it so that they may be made copies of God for His expression and glorification (see note Exo. 20:1 1 ). Proverbs, as a subsidiary to the law, instructs people how to behave and how to build themselves up according to God’s attributes, i.e., according to what God is. As a part of the holy word in God’s Holy Scriptures, Proverbs should be considered the breath of God for us to breathe in that we may receive the life supply from God ( 2 Tim. 3:16 ). Hence, we should read Proverbs by being filled with the fullness of God in our spirit ( Eph. 5:18 ; 3:19 ). Furthermore, we should read Proverbs in the New Testament Spirit of life ( Rom. 8:2 ), with our regenerated spirit, mingling prayer with our reading ( Eph. 6:17-18 ) in order to mingle the words with spirit and life (cf. John 6:63 ). While we are still living in this body, we need Proverbs to give us instructions on how to live rightly in many aspects. However, according to God’s economy Proverbs should not be used to build up the old man by cultivating our self and our natural man. Rather, we should reject self-cultivation and condemn the building up of the natural man (cf. Matt. 16:24 ; Rom. 6:6 ; Gal. 2:20 ) and come to Proverbs as a new man ( Eph. 4:22-24 ) by exercising our spirit with the Spirit to contact the word in the spirit of prayer. Then the word in Proverbs will become spirit and life to us, not to cultivate our natural man but to cultivate our regenerated new man. We must be persons who love the Lord and pursue Christ, not self-perfection (cf. Phil. 3:3-14 ), and who love the Lord’s word in the entire Bible and read it with a praying spirit, not to seek the doctrine of letters but to seek the Spirit and word of life (cf. John 5:39-40 ; 2 Cor. 3:6 ), and not to gain any help for self-cultivation but to nourish our spirit that we may live a Christian life that is perfect in the divine virtues, which are the expressions of the divine attributes. If we are such persons, this book will render us nuggets and gems to strengthen our life of pursuing Christ for the fulfillment of God’s economy in producing and building up the Body of Christ, which consummates the New Jerusalem as God’s heart’s desire and ultimate goal.

Ref: 1 Kings 4:32 ; Prov. 10:1 ; 25:1 ; Eccl. 12:9

Proverbs presents the principles for man to live a proper human life. The major principles are revering God ( Prov. 1:7 ; 3:5-10 ), needing wisdom ( vv. 20-33 ; 3:13-24 ; 4:5-9 ), honoring one’s parents ( Prov. 1:8-9 ; 3:1-2 ; 6:20 ; 30:17 ), and holding marriage in honor ( Prov. 5:1-20 ; 31:10-31 ). To revere God is to consider and regard Him in everything, never forgetting that He is the wonderful God who created us. To revere God is to fear God ( Prov. 1:7 ; 2:4-5 ; 8:13 ; 9:10 ; 10:27 ; 14:2 , 26-27 ; 15:16 , 33 a), to trust in Him ( Prov. 3:5-8 , 26 ; 16:20 ; 30:5-6 ), and to honor Him ( Prov. 3:9-10 ). Revering God stops us from doing evil. It also causes us to be touched by the sufferings of others and to show mercy and compassion to them.

Ref: Job 28:28 ; Psa. 111:10 ; Prov. 9:10 ; 1 Pet. 2:17

Revering God and honoring one’s parents are mentioned together in Proverbs ( vv. 7-9 ). In the Ten Commandments the fifth, concerning honoring one’s parents, is ranked with the first four, concerning God (see note Exo. 20:12 1 ). To honor one’s parents is nearly equal to revering God. If we revere God, we will honor our parents. See Eph. 6:2 and notes.

Heb. neshamah; translated breath in Gen. 2:7 (see note Gen. 2:7 5b ) and Job 32:8 (see notes there).

Ref: Rom. 8:16 ; 1 Cor. 2:11 ; 1 Thes. 5:23 ; Heb. 4:12

Man’s spirit is God’s lamp within man. The light shining within man’s regenerated spirit is God Himself ( 1 John 1:5 ). Just as a lamp contains light and expresses it, man’s spirit was created to contain God and express Him. In order for the divine light to shine into man’s inward parts, God’s Spirit as the oil must soak (mingle with) man’s spirit as the wick (cf. Rom. 8:16 ) and “burn” together with man’s spirit ( Rom. 12:11 ).

verses.text: And you will be like one who lies down while at sea, Or like one who lies down at the top of a mast.
verses.marked_text: And you will be like one who lies down while at sea, Or like one who lies down at the top of a mast.

verses.text: For their heart meditates violence, And their lips talk of mischief.

verses.text: Through wisdom a house is built, And by understanding it is established,

verses.text: And by knowledge the rooms are filled With all precious and pleasant riches.
verses.marked_text: And by knowledge the rooms are filled With all precious and pleasant riches.

verses.text: A wise man is strong, And a man of knowledge increases power.

verses.text: For by sound counsel you can wage your war, And in the multitude of counselors there is victory.

verses.text: Wisdom is too high for a fool; He does not open his mouth in the gate.

verses.text: He who devises to do evil, Men will call him a mischief-maker.
verses.marked_text: He who devises to do evil, Men will call him a mischief-maker.

verses.text: The devising of folly is sin, And the scorner is an abomination to men.
verses.marked_text: The devising of folly is sin, And the scorner is an abomination to men.

verses.text: If you faint in the day of adversity, Your strength is limited.
verses.marked_text: If you faint in the day of adversity, Your strength is limited.

verses.text: Deliver those who are being taken away to death, And those who are staggering to be slain, oh, hold back!

verses.text: If you say, Look, we did not know this — Does not He who weighs the hearts consider it? And He who keeps your soul, does He not know it? And will He not render to every man according to his work?

verses.text: My son, eat honey, for it is good, And the drippings from the honeycomb, which are sweet to your taste:

verses.text: Know that wisdom is such for your soul; If you find it, then there will be a latter end, And your hope will not be cut off.
verses.marked_text: Know that wisdom is such for your soul; If you find it, then there will be a latter end, And your hope will not be cut off.

verses.text: Do not lie in wait, O wicked man, against the dwelling of the righteous man; Do not destroy his resting place;
verses.marked_text: Do not lie in wait, O wicked man, against the dwelling of the righteous man; Do not destroy his resting place;

verses.text: For a righteous man falls seven times and rises up again, But the wicked are overthrown by calamity.
verses.marked_text: For a righteous man falls seven times and rises up again, But the wicked are overthrown by calamity.

verses.text: Do not rejoice when your enemy falls, And do not let your heart exult when he is overthrown;
verses.marked_text: Do not rejoice when your enemy falls, And do not let your heart exult when he is overthrown;

verses.text: Lest Jehovah see it, and it displease Him, And He turn away His anger from him.
verses.marked_text: Lest Jehovah see it, and it displease Him, And He turn away His anger from him.

verses.text: Do not be incensed because of evildoers; Do not be envious of the wicked;
verses.marked_text: Do not be incensed because of evildoers; Do not be envious of the wicked;

verses.text: For there will be no future for the evil man; The lamp of the wicked will be put out.
verses.marked_text: For there will be no future for the evil man; The lamp of the wicked will be put out.

verses.text: My son, fear Jehovah and the king, And do not associate with those who are given to change;
verses.marked_text: My son, fear Jehovah and the king, And do not associate with those who are given to change;

verses.text: For their calamity will rise suddenly, And who knows the misfortune of both of them?
verses.marked_text: For their calamity will rise suddenly, And who knows the misfortune of both of them?

verses.marked_text: These also are sayings of the wise: It is not good to have respect of persons in judgment.

verses.text: He who says to the wicked man, You are righteous, Peoples will curse him; nations will abhor him.
verses.marked_text: He who says to the wicked man, You are righteous, Peoples will curse him; nations will abhor him.

verses.text: But those who rebuke the wicked man will have delight, And a good blessing will come upon them.
verses.marked_text: But those who rebuke the wicked man will have delight, And a good blessing will come upon them.

verses.text: He who gives an honest answer Kisses the lips.
verses.marked_text: He who gives an honest answer Kisses the lips.

verses.text: Prepare your work outside, And make it ready for yourself in the field, And afterward build your house.
verses.marked_text: Prepare your work outside, And make it ready for yourself in the field, And afterward build your house.

verses.text: Do not be a witness against your neighbor without cause, And do not deceive with your lips.
verses.marked_text: Do not be a witness against your neighbor without cause, And do not deceive with your lips.

verses.text: Do not say, I will do to him as he has done to me; I will render to the man according to his work.
verses.marked_text: Do not say, I will do to him as he has done to me; I will render to the man according to his work.

verses.text: I passed by the field of the sluggard, And by the vineyard of the man lacking sense;
verses.marked_text: I passed by the field of the sluggard, And by the vineyard of the man lacking sense;

verses.text: And there it was, all overgrown with thorns; Its surface was covered with nettles, And its stone wall was broken down.

verses.text: A little sleep, a little slumber, A little folding of the hands to rest,

verses.text: And your poverty will come upon you like a robber, And your want, like an armed man.

verses.text: It is the glory of God to conceal a matter, But the glory of kings is to search a matter out.
verses.marked_text: It is the glory of God to conceal a matter, But the glory of kings is to search a matter out.

verses.text: As the heavens for height, and the earth for depth, So the heart of kings is unsearchable.
verses.marked_text: As the heavens for height, and the earth for depth, So the heart of kings is unsearchable.

verses.text: Take away the dross from the silver, And a vessel comes out for the smith;
verses.marked_text: Take away the dross from the silver, And a vessel comes out for the smith;

verses.text: Take away the wicked man from before the king, And his throne will be established in righteousness.
verses.marked_text: Take away the wicked man from before the king, And his throne will be established in righteousness.

verses.text: Do not claim honor for yourself in the presence of the king, And do not stand in the place of great men;
verses.marked_text: Do not claim honor for yourself in the presence of the king, And do not stand in the place of great men;

verses.text: For it is better that it is said to you, Come up here, Than that you should be put lower in the presence of the noble, Whom your eyes have seen.
verses.marked_text: For it is better that it is said to you, Come up here, Than that you should be put lower in the presence of the noble, Whom your eyes have seen.

verses.text: Do not go out hastily to strive; Otherwise what will you do in the end, When your neighbor puts you to shame?
verses.marked_text: Do not go out hastily to strive; Otherwise what will you do in the end, When your neighbor puts you to shame?

verses.text: Argue your case with your neighbor himself, And do not reveal the secret of another;
verses.marked_text: Argue your case with your neighbor himself, And do not reveal the secret of another;

verses.text: Lest he who hears it revile you, And the evil report of you does not go away.
verses.marked_text: Lest he who hears it revile you, And the evil report of you does not go away.

verses.text: A word fitly spoken Is like apples of gold in settings of silver.
verses.marked_text: A word fitly spoken Is like apples of gold in settings of silver.

verses.text: Like an earring of gold and an ornament of fine gold Is a wise reprover to a listening ear.
verses.marked_text: Like an earring of gold and an ornament of fine gold Is a wise reprover to a listening ear.

verses.text: Like the cold of snow in the time of harvest Is a faithful messenger to those who send him, For he refreshes the soul of his masters.
verses.marked_text: Like the cold of snow in the time of harvest Is a faithful messenger to those who send him, For he refreshes the soul of his masters.

verses.text: Like clouds and wind without rain Is one who boasts of his gifts falsely.
verses.marked_text: Like clouds and wind without rain Is one who boasts of his gifts falsely.

verses.text: By forbearance a ruler may be persuaded, And a soft tongue can break the bone.
verses.marked_text: By forbearance a ruler may be persuaded, And a soft tongue can break the bone.

verses.text: Have you found honey? Eat only what you need, Lest you become filled up with it and vomit it.
verses.marked_text: Have you found honey? Eat only what you need, Lest you become filled up with it and vomit it.

verses.text: Let your foot be seldom in your neighbor’s house, Otherwise he will become weary of you and hate you.
verses.marked_text: Let your foot be seldom in your neighbor’s house, Otherwise he will become weary of you and hate you.

verses.text: A man who bears false witness against his neighbor Is like a club and a sword and a sharp arrow.
verses.marked_text: A man who bears false witness against his neighbor Is like a club and a sword and a sharp arrow.

verses.text: Confidence in a treacherous man in time of trouble Is like a bad tooth and a foot out of joint.
verses.marked_text: Confidence in a treacherous man in time of trouble Is like a bad tooth and a foot out of joint.

verses.text: He who sings songs to a troubled heart Is like one who takes off a garment on a cold day, Or like vinegar on soda.
verses.marked_text: He who sings songs to a troubled heart Is like one who takes off a garment on a cold day, Or like vinegar on soda.

verses.text: If your enemy is hungry, give him bread to eat; And if he is thirsty, give him water to drink;
verses.marked_text: If your enemy is hungry, give him bread to eat; And if he is thirsty, give him water to drink;

verses.text: For you will heap coals of fire upon his head, And Jehovah will reward you.
verses.marked_text: For you will heap coals of fire upon his head, And Jehovah will reward you.

verses.text: The north wind brings forth rain; And a backbiting tongue, an angry countenance.
verses.marked_text: The north wind brings forth rain; And a backbiting tongue, an angry countenance.

verses.text: It is better to dwell in a corner of the housetop Than in a house shared with a contentious woman.
verses.marked_text: It is better to dwell in a corner of the housetop Than in a house shared with a contentious woman.

verses.text: Like cold water to a thirsty soul, So is good news from a far country.
verses.marked_text: Like cold water to a thirsty soul, So is good news from a far country.

verses.text: Like a muddied fountain and a polluted spring Is a righteous man who gives way before the wicked man.
verses.marked_text: Like a muddied fountain and a polluted spring Is a righteous man who gives way before the wicked man.

verses.text: It is not good to eat much honey, Nor is it glory for men to search out their own glory.
verses.marked_text: It is not good to eat much honey, Nor is it glory for men to search out their own glory.

verses.text: Like a city that is broken down, without walls, Is a man whose spirit is without restraint.
verses.marked_text: Like a city that is broken down, without walls, Is a man whose spirit is without restraint.

verses.text: Like snow in summer and like rain in harvest, So honor is not fitting for a fool.
verses.marked_text: Like snow in summer and like rain in harvest, So honor is not fitting for a fool.

verses.text: Like the sparrow in its fluttering, like the swallow in its flying, So a curse without cause does not alight.
verses.marked_text: Like the sparrow in its fluttering, like the swallow in its flying, So a curse without cause does not alight.

verses.text: A whip for the horse! A bridle for the donkey! And a rod for the back of fools!
verses.marked_text: A whip for the horse! A bridle for the donkey! And a rod for the back of fools!

verses.text: Do not answer a fool according to his folly, Lest you also be like him.
verses.marked_text: Do not answer a fool according to his folly, Lest you also be like him.

verses.text: Answer a fool according to his folly, Lest he be wise in his own eyes.
verses.marked_text: Answer a fool according to his folly, Lest he be wise in his own eyes.

verses.text: He who sends a message by the hand of a fool Cuts off his own feet and drinks violence.
verses.marked_text: He who sends a message by the hand of a fool Cuts off his own feet and drinks violence.

verses.marked_text: Like the legs of the lame which hang down, So is a proverb in the mouth of fools.

verses.text: Like one who binds a stone in a sling, So is he who gives honor to a fool.
verses.marked_text: Like one who binds a stone in a sling, So is he who gives honor to a fool.

verses.text: Like a thorn that goes up into the hand of a drunkard, So is a proverb in the mouth of fools.
verses.marked_text: Like a thorn that goes up into the hand of a drunkard, So is a proverb in the mouth of fools.

verses.text: Like an archer who wounds everyone, So is he who hires a fool or who hires those who pass by.
verses.marked_text: Like an archer who wounds everyone, So is he who hires a fool or who hires those who pass by.

verses.text: Like a dog that returns to its vomit Is a fool who repeats his folly.
verses.marked_text: Like a dog that returns to its vomit Is a fool who repeats his folly.

verses.text: Do you see a man who is wise in his own eyes? There is more hope for a fool than for him.
verses.marked_text: Do you see a man who is wise in his own eyes? There is more hope for a fool than for him.

verses.text: The sluggard says, There is a roaring lion on the way; A lion is in the streets!
verses.marked_text: The sluggard says, There is a roaring lion on the way; A lion is in the streets!

verses.text: As the door turns upon its hinges, So does the sluggard upon his bed.
verses.marked_text: As the door turns upon its hinges, So does the sluggard upon his bed.

verses.text: The sluggard buries his hand in the dish; He gets weary by bringing it to his mouth again.
verses.marked_text: The sluggard buries his hand in the dish; He gets weary by bringing it to his mouth again.

verses.text: The sluggard is wiser in his own eyes Than seven men who can answer discreetly.
verses.marked_text: The sluggard is wiser in his own eyes Than seven men who can answer discreetly.

verses.text: He who passes by and meddles with strife that does not belong to him, Is like one who takes a dog by the ears.
verses.marked_text: He who passes by and meddles with strife that does not belong to him, Is like one who takes a dog by the ears.

verses.text: Like a madman who shoots firebrands, arrows, and death,
verses.marked_text: Like a madman who shoots firebrands, arrows, and death,

verses.text: So is the man who deceives his neighbor, And says, Was I not joking?
verses.marked_text: So is the man who deceives his neighbor, And says, Was I not joking?

verses.text: For lack of wood the fire goes out, And where there is no whisperer, contention quiets down.
verses.marked_text: For lack of wood the fire goes out, And where there is no whisperer, contention quiets down.

verses.text: As charcoal to hot embers and wood to fire, So is a contentious man to kindle strife.
verses.marked_text: As charcoal to hot embers and wood to fire, So is a contentious man to kindle strife.

verses.text: The words of a whisperer are like dainty morsels, And they go down into the innermost parts of one’s being.
verses.marked_text: The words of a whisperer are like dainty morsels, And they go down into the innermost parts of one’s being.

verses.text: Burning lips and a wicked heart Are like an earthen vessel overlaid with silver dross.
verses.marked_text: Burning lips and a wicked heart Are like an earthen vessel overlaid with silver dross.

verses.text: He who hates disguises it with his lips, But he lays up deceit within him;
verses.marked_text: He who hates disguises it with his lips, But he lays up deceit within him;

verses.text: When he speaks graciously, do not believe him; For there are seven abominations in his heart;
verses.marked_text: When he speaks graciously, do not believe him; For there are seven abominations in his heart;

verses.text: Though his hatred covers itself with guile, His wickedness will be revealed before the assembly.
verses.marked_text: Though his hatred covers itself with guile, His wickedness will be revealed before the assembly.

verses.text: Whoever digs a pit will fall into it, And he who rolls a stone, it will come back on him.
verses.marked_text: Whoever digs a pit will fall into it, And he who rolls a stone, it will come back on him.

verses.text: A lying tongue hates those it crushes, And a flattering mouth works ruin.
verses.marked_text: A lying tongue hates those it crushes, And a flattering mouth works ruin.

verses.text: Do not boast about tomorrow, For you do not know what a day may bring forth.
verses.marked_text: Do not boast about tomorrow, For you do not know what a day may bring forth.

verses.text: Let another praise you, and not your own mouth; A foreigner, and not your own lips.
verses.marked_text: Let another praise you, and not your own mouth; A foreigner, and not your own lips.

verses.marked_text: A stone is heavy, and the sand weighty, But a fool’s vexation is heavier than both of them.

verses.text: Wrath is cruel, and anger is overwhelming, But who can stand before jealousy?
verses.marked_text: Wrath is cruel, and anger is overwhelming, But who can stand before jealousy?

verses.text: Open rebuke is better Than love that is hidden.
verses.marked_text: Open rebuke is better Than love that is hidden.

verses.text: Faithful are the wounds of a friend, But the kisses of an enemy are profuse.
verses.marked_text: Faithful are the wounds of a friend, But the kisses of an enemy are profuse.

verses.text: The full soul loathes a honeycomb, But to the hungry soul every bitter thing is sweet.
verses.marked_text: The full soul loathes a honeycomb, But to the hungry soul every bitter thing is sweet.

verses.text: Like a bird that wanders from her nest, So is a man who wanders from his place.
verses.marked_text: Like a bird that wanders from her nest, So is a man who wanders from his place.

verses.text: Oil and perfume rejoice the heart; So a man’s counsel is sweet to his friend.
verses.marked_text: Oil and perfume rejoice the heart; So a man’s counsel is sweet to his friend.

verses.text: Do not forsake your own friend or your father’s friend To go to your brother’s house in the day of your calamity: Better is a neighbor who is near than a brother far away.
verses.marked_text: Do not forsake your own friend or your father’s friend To go to your brother’s house in the day of your calamity: Better is a neighbor who is near than a brother far away.

verses.text: My son, be wise, and make my heart glad, That I may answer him who reproaches me.

verses.marked_text: A prudent man sees evil and hides himself; But the simple pass on and suffer punishment for it.

verses.marked_text: Take the garment of him who is surety for a stranger, And hold one in pledge who is surety for a foreign woman.

verses.marked_text: He who blesses his friend with a loud voice, Arousing him early in the morning, It will be reckoned as a curse to him.

verses.marked_text: A continual dripping on a very rainy day And a contentious woman are alike;

verses.text: He who would restrain her restrains the wind, And grasps oil with his right hand.
verses.marked_text: He who would restrain her restrains the wind, And grasps oil with his right hand.

verses.text: Iron sharpens iron; So a man sharpens the countenance of his friend.
verses.marked_text: Iron sharpens iron; So a man sharpens the countenance of his friend.

verses.text: Whoever tends a fig tree will eat its fruit, And he who takes care of his master will be honored.
verses.marked_text: Whoever tends a fig tree will eat its fruit, And he who takes care of his master will be honored.

verses.text: As in water face reflects face, So the heart of man reflects man.
verses.marked_text: As in water face reflects face, So the heart of man reflects man.

verses.text: Sheol and Abaddon are never satisfied, And the eyes of man are never satisfied.
verses.marked_text: Sheol and Abaddon<fn n="1"/> are never satisfied, And the eyes of man are never satisfied.

verses.marked_text: The refining pot is for silver and the furnace for gold, And a man is tried by the praise given him.

verses.text: For riches are not forever, Nor does a crown endure from generation to generation —

verses.marked_text: Like a roaring lion and a roving bear Is a wicked ruler over a poor people.

verses.text: The ruler who lacks understanding is also a great oppressor, But he who hates unjust gain will prolong his days.
verses.marked_text: The ruler who lacks understanding is also a great oppressor, But he who hates unjust gain will prolong his days.

verses.text: A man who is burdened with a person’s blood Will be a fugitive until death; Let no man support him.
verses.marked_text: A man who is burdened with a person’s blood Will<fn n="1"/> be a fugitive until death; Let no man support him.

verses.text: Whoever walks uprightly will be delivered, But he who is perverse in his ways will fall all at once.
verses.marked_text: Whoever walks uprightly will be delivered, But he who is perverse in his ways will fall all at once.

verses.text: He who tills his land will have plenty of bread, But he who pursues worthless things will have plenty of poverty.
verses.marked_text: He who tills his land will have plenty of bread, But he who pursues worthless things will have plenty of poverty.

verses.text: A faithful man will abound with blessings, But he who makes haste to be rich will not go unpunished.
verses.marked_text: A faithful man will abound with blessings, But he who makes haste to be rich will not go unpunished.

verses.text: To have respect of persons is not good, Because for a piece of bread a man will transgress.
verses.marked_text: To have respect of persons is not good, Because for a piece of bread a man will transgress.

verses.text: A man who is envious hastens after wealth, And does not know that want will come upon him.
verses.marked_text: A man who is envious hastens after wealth, And does not know that want will come upon him.

verses.text: He who rebukes a man will afterward find more favor Than he who flatters with the tongue.
verses.marked_text: He who rebukes a man will afterward find more favor Than he who flatters with the tongue.

verses.text: Whoever robs his father or his mother and says, It is no transgression, Is the companion of a man who destroys.
verses.marked_text: Whoever robs his father or his mother and says, It is no transgression, Is the companion of a man who destroys.

verses.text: A greedy person stirs up contention, But he who trusts in Jehovah will prosper.
verses.marked_text: A greedy person stirs up contention, But he who trusts in Jehovah will prosper.

verses.text: He who trusts in his own heart is a fool, But he who walks wisely will be delivered.
verses.marked_text: He who trusts in his own heart is a fool, But he who walks wisely will be delivered.

verses.text: He who gives to the poor man will not lack, But he who shuts his eyes will have many curses.
verses.marked_text: He who gives to the poor man will not lack, But he who shuts his eyes will have many curses.

verses.text: When the wicked rise, men hide themselves; But when they perish, the righteous increase.
verses.marked_text: When the wicked rise, men hide themselves; But when they perish, the righteous increase.

verses.text: He who hardens his neck after being often reproved Will suddenly be broken beyond remedy.
verses.marked_text: He who hardens his neck after being often reproved Will suddenly be broken beyond remedy.

verses.text: When the righteous increase, the people rejoice; But when a wicked man rules, the people groan.
verses.marked_text: When the righteous increase, the people rejoice; But when a wicked man rules, the people groan.

verses.text: Whoever loves wisdom makes his father glad, But he who keeps company with harlots wastes his substance.
verses.marked_text: Whoever loves wisdom makes his father glad, But he who keeps company with harlots wastes his substance.

verses.text: The king by justice establishes the land, But a man who takes bribes overthrows it.
verses.marked_text: The king by justice establishes the land, But a man who takes bribes overthrows it.

verses.text: A man who flatters his neighbor Spreads a net for his steps.
verses.marked_text: A man who flatters his neighbor Spreads a net for his steps.

verses.text: In the transgression of an evil man there is a snare, But the righteous man sings and rejoices.
verses.marked_text: In the transgression of an evil man there is a snare, But the righteous man sings and rejoices.

verses.text: The righteous man knows the rights of the poor; The wicked man has no understanding of such knowledge.
verses.marked_text: The righteous man knows the rights of the poor; The wicked man has no understanding of such knowledge.

verses.text: Scorners set a city aflame, But wise men turn away wrath.
verses.marked_text: Scorners set a city aflame, But wise men turn away wrath.

verses.text: If a wise man has a controversy with a foolish man, The fool is either angry or laughs, and there is no rest.
verses.marked_text: If a wise man has a controversy with a foolish man, The fool is either angry or laughs, and there is no rest.

verses.text: The bloodthirsty hate one who is perfect, And they seek the life of the upright.
verses.marked_text: The bloodthirsty hate one who is perfect, And they seek the life of the upright.

verses.text: A fool utters all his anger, But a wise man holds it back.
verses.marked_text: A fool utters all his anger, But a wise man holds it back.

verses.text: If a ruler pays attention to a false word, All his servants are wicked.
verses.marked_text: If a ruler pays attention to a false word, All his servants are wicked.

verses.text: The poor man and the oppressor have this in common: Jehovah gives light to the eyes of them both.
verses.marked_text: The poor man and the oppressor have this in common: Jehovah gives light to the eyes of them both.

verses.text: If a king judges the poor in truth, His throne will be established forever.
verses.marked_text: If a king judges the poor in truth, His throne will be established forever.

verses.text: The rod and reproof give wisdom, But a child left to himself brings shame to his mother.
verses.marked_text: The rod and reproof give wisdom, But a child left to himself brings shame to his mother.

verses.text: When the wicked increase, transgression increases; But the righteous will see their fall.
verses.marked_text: When the wicked increase, transgression increases; But the righteous will see their fall.

verses.text: Correct your son, and he will give you rest; He will also give delight to your soul.
verses.marked_text: Correct your son, and he will give you rest; He will also give delight to your soul.

verses.text: Where there is no vision, the people cast off restraint; But happy is he who keeps the law.
verses.marked_text: Where there is no vision, the people cast off restraint; But happy is he who keeps the law.

verses.text: A servant will not be corrected by words alone; For though he understands, there will be no response.
verses.marked_text: A servant will not be corrected by words alone; For though he understands, there will be no response.

verses.text: Do you see a man who is hasty in his words? There is more hope for a fool than for him.
verses.marked_text: Do you see a man who is hasty in his words? There is more hope for a fool than for him.

verses.text: He who delicately brings up his servant from a child Will have him as a son in the end.
verses.marked_text: He who delicately brings up his servant from a child Will have him as a son in the end.

verses.text: An angry man stirs up contention, And a furious man abounds in transgression.
verses.marked_text: An angry man stirs up contention, And a furious man abounds in transgression.

verses.text: A man’s pride will bring him low, But he who is of a lowly spirit will obtain honor.
verses.marked_text: A man’s pride will bring him low, But he who is of a lowly spirit will obtain honor.

verses.text: Whoever is partner with a thief hates his own soul; He hears the adjuration and utters nothing.
verses.marked_text: Whoever is partner with a thief hates his own soul; He hears the adjuration and utters nothing.

verses.text: The fear of man brings a snare, But whoever puts his trust in Jehovah will be exalted.
verses.marked_text: The fear of man brings a snare, But whoever puts his trust in Jehovah will be exalted<fn n="1"/>.

verses.text: Many seek the ruler’s favor, But justice for man comes from Jehovah.
verses.marked_text: Many seek the ruler’s favor, But justice for man comes from Jehovah.

verses.text: An unjust man is an abomination to the righteous, And he who is upright in the way is an abomination to the wicked man.
verses.marked_text: An unjust man is an abomination to the righteous, And he who is upright in the way is an abomination to the wicked man.

outlines.text: III. The word of Agur — general words of wisdom (30:1-33)

verses.text: The words of Agur the son of Jakeh. The oracle. The man declares to Ithiel, to Ithiel and Ucal:
verses.marked_text: The words of Agur the son of Jakeh. The oracle. The man declares to Ithiel, to Ithiel and Ucal:
outlines: III. The word of Agur — general words of wisdom (30:1-33)

verses.text: Surely I am more stupid than any man, And do not have a man’s understanding;
verses.marked_text: Surely I am more stupid than any man, And do not have a man’s understanding;

verses.text: And I have not learned wisdom, Nor do I have the knowledge of the Holy One.
verses.marked_text: And I have not learned wisdom, Nor do I have the knowledge of the Holy One.

verses.text: Who has ascended into heaven and descended? Who has gathered the wind in His fists? Who has wrapped up the waters in His garment? Who has established all the ends of the earth? What is His name, and what is His Son’s name, if you know?
verses.marked_text: Who has ascended into heaven and descended? Who has gathered the wind in His fists? Who has wrapped up the waters in His garment? Who has established all the ends of the earth? What is His name, and what is His Son’s name, if you know?

verses.text: Every word of God is tried; He is a shield to those who take refuge in Him.
verses.marked_text: Every word of God is tried; He is a shield to those who take refuge in Him.

verses.text: Do not add to His words, Lest He reprove you and you be found a liar.
verses.marked_text: Do not add to His words, Lest He reprove you and you be found a liar.

verses.text: Two things I have asked of You; Do not refuse me before I die:
verses.marked_text: Two things I have asked of You; Do not refuse me before I die:

verses.text: Remove far from me falsehood and lies. Give me neither poverty nor riches; Feed me with the food that is my portion,
verses.marked_text: Remove far from me falsehood and lies. Give me neither poverty nor riches; Feed me with the food that is my portion,

verses.text: Lest I become full and deny You and say, Who is Jehovah? Or lest I become poor and steal and profane the name of my God.
verses.marked_text: Lest I become full and deny You and say, Who is Jehovah? Or lest I become poor and steal and profane the name of my God.

verses.text: Do not slander a servant to his master, Lest he curse you, and you be held guilty.
verses.marked_text: Do not slander a servant to his master, Lest he curse you, and you be held guilty.

verses.text: There is a generation that curse their father, And do not bless their mother.
verses.marked_text: There is a generation that curse their father, And do not bless their mother.

verses.text: There is a generation that are pure in their own eyes, And yet are not washed from their filthiness.
verses.marked_text: There is a generation that are pure in their own eyes, And yet are not washed from their filthiness.

verses.text: There is a generation — oh how lofty are their eyes, And their eyelids are raised arrogantly.
verses.marked_text: There is a generation — oh how lofty are their eyes, And their eyelids are raised arrogantly.

verses.text: There is a generation whose teeth are like swords, And their jaw teeth like knives, To devour the afflicted from off the earth, And the needy from among men.
verses.marked_text: There is a generation whose teeth are like swords, And their jaw teeth like knives, To devour the afflicted from off the earth, And the needy from among men.

verses.text: The leech has two daughters, crying, Give, give. There are three things that are never satisfied, Indeed, four that do not say, Enough:
verses.marked_text: The leech has two daughters, crying, Give, give. There are three things that are never satisfied, Indeed, four that do not say, Enough:

verses.text: Sheol and the barren womb, The earth that is not satisfied with water, And the fire that does not say, Enough.
verses.marked_text: Sheol and the barren womb, The earth that is not satisfied with water, And the fire that does not say, Enough.

verses.text: The eye that mocks his father And despises to obey his mother, The ravens of the valley will pick it out, And the young eagles will eat it.
verses.marked_text: The eye that mocks his father And despises to obey his mother, The ravens of the valley will pick it out, And the young eagles will eat it.

verses.text: There are three things which are too wonderful for me, Indeed four which I do not know:
verses.marked_text: There are three things which are too wonderful for me, Indeed four which I do not know:

verses.text: The way of an eagle in the sky, The way of a serpent upon a rock, The way of a ship in the midst of the sea, And the way of a man with a maiden.
verses.marked_text: The way of an eagle in the sky, The way of a serpent upon a rock, The way of a ship in the midst of the sea, And the way of a man with a maiden.

verses.text: This is the way of an adulterous woman: She eats and wipes her mouth And says, I have done no wickedness.
verses.marked_text: This is the way of an adulterous woman: She eats and wipes her mouth And says, I have done no wickedness.

verses.text: Under three things the earth quakes, And under four, it cannot bear up:
verses.marked_text: Under three things the earth quakes, And under four, it cannot bear up:

verses.text: Under a servant when he is king, And a fool when he is filled with food;
verses.marked_text: Under a servant when he is king, And a fool when he is filled with food;

verses.text: Under a hated woman when she gets married, And a servant girl who is heir to her mistress.
verses.marked_text: Under a hated woman when she gets married, And a servant girl who is heir to her mistress.

verses.text: Four things are small on the earth, But they are exceedingly wise:
verses.marked_text: Four things are small on the earth, But they are exceedingly wise:

verses.text: The ants are a clan without strength, Yet they prepare their food in the summer;
verses.marked_text: The ants are a clan without strength, Yet they prepare their food in the summer;

verses.text: The rock badgers are a clan without might, Yet they make their houses in the rocks;
verses.marked_text: The rock badgers are a clan without might, Yet they make their houses in the rocks;

verses.text: The swarming locusts have no king, Yet all of them go out in ranks;
verses.marked_text: The swarming locusts have no king, Yet all of them go out in ranks;

verses.text: The lizard can be grasped with the hands, Yet she is in kings’ palaces.
verses.marked_text: The lizard can be grasped with the hands, Yet she is in kings’ palaces.

verses.text: There are three things which are stately in their step, Indeed four which are stately in walking:
verses.marked_text: There are three things which are stately in their step, Indeed four which are stately in walking:

verses.text: The lion, which is mightiest among beasts, And does not turn back before any;
verses.marked_text: The lion, which is mightiest among beasts, And does not turn back before any;

verses.text: The strutting cock girded in the loins, or a male goat, And a king who has a band of soldiers with him.
verses.marked_text: The strutting cock girded in the loins, or a male goat, And a king who has a band of soldiers with him.

verses.text: If you have been foolish in exalting yourself, Or if you have thought an evil scheme, Put your hand upon your mouth.
verses.marked_text: If you have been foolish in exalting yourself, Or if you have thought an evil scheme, Put your hand upon your mouth.

verses.text: For the churning of milk produces butter, And the wringing of the nose brings forth blood, So the pressing of wrath brings forth strife.
verses.marked_text: For the churning of milk produces butter, And the wringing of the nose brings forth blood, So the pressing of wrath brings forth strife.

verses.text: What, my son? and what, O son of my womb? And what, O son of my vows?
verses.marked_text: What, my son? and what, O son of my womb? And what, O son of my vows?

verses.text: Do not give your strength to women, Nor your ways to that which destroys kings.
verses.marked_text: Do not give your strength to women, Nor your ways to that which destroys kings.

verses.text: It is not for kings, O Lemuel, it is not for kings to drink wine; Nor for princes to say, Where is strong drink?
verses.marked_text: It is not for kings, O Lemuel, it is not for kings to drink wine; Nor for princes to say, Where is strong drink?

verses.text: Lest they drink and forget what is decreed, And pervert the rights of all the afflicted.
verses.marked_text: Lest they drink and forget what is decreed, And pervert the rights of all the afflicted.

verses.text: Give strong drink rather to one who is perishing, And wine to the bitter in soul;
verses.marked_text: Give strong drink rather to one who is perishing, And wine to the bitter in soul;

verses.text: Let him drink and forget his poverty, And remember his misery no more.
verses.marked_text: Let him drink and forget his poverty, And remember his misery no more.

verses.text: Open your mouth for the dumb, And for the rights of all those who are passing away.
verses.marked_text: Open your mouth for the dumb, And for the rights of all those who are passing away.

verses.text: Open your mouth; judge righteously, And minister justice to the poor and needy.
verses.marked_text: Open your mouth; judge righteously, And minister justice to the poor and needy.

verses.text: Who can find a worthy woman? For her price is far above corals.
verses.marked_text: Who can find a worthy woman? For her price is far above corals.

verses.text: The heart of her husband trusts in her, And he will have no lack of gain.
verses.marked_text: The heart of her husband trusts in her, And he will have no lack of gain.

verses.text: She does him good and not evil All the days of her life.
verses.marked_text: She does him good and not evil All the days of her life.

verses.text: She seeks wool and flax, And delights to work with her hands.
verses.marked_text: She seeks wool and flax, And delights to work with her hands.

verses.text: She is like the merchant ships; She brings her food from afar.
verses.marked_text: She is like the merchant ships; She brings her food from afar.

verses.text: She rises also while it is still night And gives food to her household, And their task to her serving girls.
verses.marked_text: She rises also while it is still night And gives food to her household, And their task to her serving girls.

verses.text: She considers a field and buys it; With the fruit of her hands she plants a vineyard.
verses.marked_text: She considers a field and buys it; With the fruit of her hands she plants a vineyard.

verses.text: She girds her loins with strength And makes strong her arms.
verses.marked_text: She girds her loins with strength And makes strong her arms.

verses.text: She samples her merchandise to be sure it is good; Her lamp does not go out by night.
verses.marked_text: She samples her merchandise to be sure it is good; Her lamp does not go out by night.

verses.text: She lays her hands to the distaff, And her hands hold on to the spindle.
verses.marked_text: She lays her hands to the distaff, And her hands hold on to the spindle.

verses.text: She stretches out her hand to the afflicted, And she reaches out her hands to the needy.
verses.marked_text: She stretches out her hand to the afflicted, And she reaches out her hands to the needy.

verses.text: She does not fear for her household when it snows, For all her household are clothed with scarlet.
verses.marked_text: She does not fear for her household when it snows, For all her household are clothed with scarlet.

verses.text: She makes coverings for herself; Her clothing is fine linen and purple.
verses.marked_text: She makes coverings for herself; Her clothing is fine linen and purple.

verses.text: Her husband is known in the gates, When he sits among the elders of the land.
verses.marked_text: Her husband is known in the gates, When he sits among the elders of the land.

verses.text: She makes linen garments and sells them And delivers girdles to the merchant.
verses.marked_text: She makes linen garments and sells them And delivers girdles to the merchant.

verses.text: Strength and dignity are her clothing, And she happily looks forward to the time to come.
verses.marked_text: Strength and dignity are her clothing, And she happily looks forward to the time to come.

verses.text: She opens her mouth with wisdom, And the law of kindness is on her tongue.
verses.marked_text: She opens her mouth with wisdom, And the law<fn n="1"/> of kindness is on her tongue.

verses.text: She watches closely over the ways of her household And does not eat the bread of idleness.
verses.marked_text: She watches closely over the ways of her household And does not eat the bread of idleness.

verses.text: Her children rise up and call her blessed; Her husband also, and he praises her, saying:
verses.marked_text: Her children rise up and call her blessed; Her husband also, and he praises her, saying:

verses.text: Many daughters have done worthily, But you surpass them all.
verses.marked_text: Many daughters have done worthily, But you surpass them all.

verses.text: Grace is deceitful, and beauty is vain; But a woman who fears Jehovah, she will be praised.
verses.marked_text: Grace is deceitful, and beauty is vain; But a woman who fears Jehovah, she will be praised.

verses.text: Give her of the fruit of her hands, And let her works praise her in the gates.
verses.marked_text: Give her of the fruit of her hands, And let her works praise her in the gates.
